Activity: Exploring Endangered Wildlife in Nepal Objective: Students will research endangered wildlife in Nepal and understand the role of IUCN. Materials Required: − Access to the internet for research. − Paper and pens for notes. − Projector or whiteboard for presentations Procedure: i. Briefly explain the importance of biodiversity and endangered species. ii. Introduce the IUCN and its role in conservation. iii. Divide students into small groups. iv. Assign each group one endangered animal species in Nepal (e.g., Bengal Tiger, Red Panda, Great Hornbill). v. Assist them with some guiding research questions: o What is the habitat of this species? o What are the main threats to its survival? o What is the current population status according to the IUCN Red List? o What conservation efforts are in place to protect this species?
vi. Each group prepares a brief presentation (about 3 minutes) summarizing their
vii. Groups present their research to the class.
Encourage questions and discussions after each presentation.
